content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated GPU paging and OOM rates detected in runtime-pool-east (region us-east1). 18% of requests experiencing >400ms stall for KV swap. Investigating.

jamie: I'm on it, grabbing logs and starting handoff with oncall.

anita: hey @jamie @sre-oncall — seeing a customer spike from priority customers 2 and 3? any impact telemetry?

jamie: preliminary dashboards show increased page fault rates starting ~2278901100, concurrent OOMs on g4dn-type instances, some vmem churn. Not all requests fail but latency and retrys up.

sre-oncall: oncall takeover — I’m going to coordinate mitigation. Who has fresh kvmalloc/log snippets?

lee: pushed a quick scrub, attaching recent nvidia-smi from 3 affected GPUs:
```
GPU 0: 48% mem, processes: runtime-server (pid 14231) mem 6.2G
GPU 1: 98% mem, processes: runtime-server (pid 15322) mem 12.6G
GPU 2: 77% mem, processes: runtime-server (pid 15877) mem 9.8G
Page faults/sec: spike to 2400 -> normal 120
```

carl: also saw a pattern in the runtime logs -> repeated KV cache eviction + rehydrate loop. snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T11:05:02Z] kvcache: evict shard=7 size=512MB reason=pressure
[2026-03-14T11:05:02Z] runtime: request start id=abcd seq=14 batch=8
[2026-03-14T11:05:02Z] kvcache: miss shard=7 key=... rehydrate from remote
[2026-03-14T11:05:04Z] runtime: retry due to prefault delay
```

maria: customer-facing: a handful of sessions reported timeouts, but we haven't seen a major outage page yet. APM traces show tail latency jumps for embedding endpoints.

eng-runtime: hypothesis: tight batch sizing + large KV cache churn causing frequent page-ins; model context sizes increased for a subset of requests (long prompts). Combined effect pushes some GPUs into fragmentation and swap.

jamie: timeline I'm building:
- 2278901050: normal baseline
- 2278901105: small traffic surge from an internal perf test
- 2278901112: page fault rate climbs
- 2278901128: first OOM observed on runtime-1
- 2278901135: paging spikes across pool
- 2278901148: retries and customer timeouts appear
- 2278901220: mitigation actions started (see below)

anita: mitigation steps in-flight:
1) reduce max_batch_size from 16 -> 8 on affected shards
2) temporarily disable KV prefetch for non-verified customers
3) spin up 2 extra nodes in pool (scale-out)
4) soft-restart of runtime process on GPU1 (non-drain restart)

lee: applying change 1 now on runtime-1 and runtime-2. Patch: `--max-batch=8` via rollout config.

eng-runtime: advise to also lower `kvcache.max_active_rehydrates` from 32 -> 8 to avoid concurrent backend fetch storms.

carl: doing that now (rolling) — will take effect per process.

sre-oncall: monitoring for changes. If paging rates drop, we can keep nodes but if OOMs persist we'll need to evacuate and reprovision with larger instance types.

incident-bot: Deploy job ci/rollouts/runtime-config/2278901234 completed with status: partial. 6/10 instances updated.

jamie: update after action: page faults/sec down from 2400 -> 600 over 3 minutes, GPU1 mem usage dropping to 84% (from 98%). Some requests still hitting 300-400ms stalls.

maria: customers reporting improved behavior but a few still see retries. I'll keep CS notified and flag any priority escalations.

eng-runtime: collecting heap/dma stats from affected processes; attaching a short dump below (sanitized):
```
runtime heap: total_alloc=18.4G rss=13.2G free_segments=24
kvcache shards: active=14 rehydrates_inflight=26 avg_rehydrate_latency=420ms
fragmentation: free_blocks_small=320 large=12 external_frag=8%
```

anita: interesting that external_frag low, but rehydrate concurrency high -> suggests eviction thrash not fragmentation-only. Could be a workload with many long contexts causing repeated cache churn.

lee: one more data point: batch size distribution for last 10k requests shows long-tail: 87% batches <=8, but 3% spike to batch=32 (internal test). Those spikes line up with start of issue.

eng-runtime: tentative root cause hypothesis list (tracking):
- H1: Internal perf test caused sudden long-context requests -> batch and kvcache pressure -> rehydrates -> paging and OOM cascade
- H2: Regression in kvcache eviction policy increased rehydrate concurrency (bug) -> backend thrash and pressure
- H3: Kernel-level GPU allocator fragmentation combined with large locked allocations -> sudden OOMs on worst-fit nodes

carl: marking evidence links:
- logs: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2278901234/runtime.log.gz
- metrics: grafana/dashboard/runtime-pool-east?from=2278901000&to=2278901300
- nvidia dumps: internal-share/gpu_dumps/2278901234/

jamie: customer impact note for post-incident: ~45 customers experienced increased tail latency, 7 customers had transient request failures (auto-retries succeeded). No data exfiltration.

sre-oncall: next steps for the incident thread:
- Complete timeline + attach logs (jamie)
- Root cause deep-dive (eng-runtime + eng-ml) to confirm H1 vs H2 (eng-runtime)
- Create mitigation playbook: reduce default max_batch, kvcache concurrency caps, autoscale thresholds (SRE)
- Postmortem doc and customer comms draft (maria + trust)

eng-runtime: starting a follow-on debug run to repro by replaying offending traces at small scale. Will capture allocator traces and kvcache metrics.

maria: I'll draft a status update to affected customers: "We've mitigated the immediate issue. We're investigating root cause and will share an RCA." Will coordinate wording with legal if needed.

anita: agree — also recommend adding a short-term instrumentation (per-request context length tag) to help detect future long-context spikes.

jamie: adding incident ticket: https://tracker.redwood.ai/INC-4892 (RCA in progress)

incident-bot: Reminder: handoff checklist -- add timeline, docs, mitigation steps. Next update due in 60m.

sre-oncall: closing live mitigation loop for now; placing incident into post-incident tracking. If anything regresses ping @sre-oncall immediately. Thanks all for quick responses. :raised_hands:

jamie: thanks — saving logs and creating the RCA draft now.

eng-runtime: final note: patch to kvcache rehydrate limiter (reduce default) will be queued with high priority. Expect PR in ~3 hours.

maria: will sync on customer comms after PR lands and we validate fix in staging.

anita: wrap-up: severity reduced, customer impact limited, RCA steps assigned. I'll convert this thread into the incident timeline section for the postmortem.

sre-oncall: good work everyone.
